answer.evidence: The trunk, roof and hood form a tall top-surface stack in rows 2-40. Light bands at rows 9, 25 and 39-40 act as front-edge lines, each followed by darker shadow rows (windshield and window glass at 10-14 and 26-33). Below row 41 the vertical south face shows the grille, headlights and bumper over about 21 rows, down to row 62. No receding side face is drawn. The top surface is large, but a top and a front face of more than 3 rows are both present.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 20 visible tones per 16x16 tile, the same as prop-well-roofed (20) and above prop-stall-cheese (17) and prop-hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no 5x5 flat fills. Only 1% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is a dark teal or green tint of the body rather than a black sticker line. The body shows about 5 lightness steps across the teal panels, with rust patches, crack lines on the glass and a shaded grille and bumper. Texture and grain are comparable to the roofed well and the cheese stall. The piece is a little vertical and boxy, but that is a composition quibble and not a shading shortfall. An artist would accept it next to the references.
